item.title: Rayan Rupert's Surprising Rise: From Blazers Cast-Off to Grizzlies Starter
item.description:
What happens when an NBA team gives up on a 21-year-old too soon? The Memphis Grizzlies might have found the answer — and the Portland Trail Blazers might be regretting the question.

Rayan Rupert, the French-born guard-forward who was waived by Portland in February 2026, has quietly transformed into a legitimate rotation piece for Memphis. In just five starts with the Grizzlies, he’s averaging 10.4 points and 5.8 rebounds in 26.8 minutes per game — numbers that dwarf anything he produced in Portland.

item.title: Spurs Game Tonight: San Antonio's Dominant 57-Win Season and What Comes Next
item.description:
The Spurs Are the NBA’s Most Surprising Powerhouse — and They’re Not Slowing Down

Just two seasons removed from the league’s worst record, the San Antonio Spurs have stormed to a 57–18 record and the No. 2 seed in the Western Conference. With a nine-game winning streak and the Southwest Division already clinched, this team has gone from rebuild to contender faster than anyone predicted.

Key Takeaways

  • The Spurs sit at 57–18, No. 2 in the West, with a 9-game winning streak
  • San Antonio has clinched the Southwest Division title
  • Victor Wembanyama’s health has been a storyline heading into late-season matchups
  • The Warriors, at 36–39, have struggled without Stephen Curry (out 26 straight games)
  • Curry is targeting a return for Houston on Sunday after clearing five-on-five scrimmage work

If you haven’t been paying attention to San Antonio this season, now is the time. Here’s everything you need to know about the Spurs’ remarkable campaign, their recent stretch of games, and what it all means heading into the playoffs.

item.title: Pistons vs Timberwolves: Eastern Conference Leaders Battle Through Injury Crisis
item.description:
Can a team missing its best player still be the most dangerous squad in the NBA? The Detroit Pistons are making a compelling case.

Quick Summary:

  • The Detroit Pistons (53-20) faced the Minnesota Timberwolves (45-28) on Saturday, March 28, at Target Center in Minneapolis.
  • Both teams were missing their star guards: Cade Cunningham (collapsed lung) and Anthony Edwards (right knee).
  • Jalen Duren has emerged as a dominant force, averaging 23.7 points on 66.5% shooting with 11 rebounds over his last 19 games.
  • Detroit’s magic number to clinch the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference is just five over the Boston Celtics.

Pistons vs Timberwolves: A Clash of Playoff Contenders

The Pistons vs Timberwolves matchup on Saturday, March 28, carried serious playoff implications despite both rosters being battered by injuries. Detroit, holders of the best record in the Eastern Conference at 53-20, traveled to Minneapolis to face the fifth-seeded Timberwolves (45-28) in a nationally televised ABC game at 5:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Grayson Allen Returns: Suns Get Essential Boost for Nuggets Showdown
item.description:
Can a single player’s return flip a team’s fortunes? The Phoenix Suns are betting on it. Grayson Allen has been cleared to play Tuesday night against the Denver Nuggets after missing the Suns’ previous four games due to left knee injury management — and his comeback couldn’t come at a more critical time.

Key Takeaways

  • Grayson Allen is officially available for Tuesday’s Suns-Nuggets matchup after a four-game absence
  • Allen is posting career-high numbers this season: 17.2 points per game on 35.4% from three
  • Royce O’Neale also returns after missing three games, giving Phoenix two key rotation pieces back
  • The Suns have been battling a mounting injury list that has sidelined Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, and others at various points

Grayson Allen’s Return Changes the Equation

Allen appeared to be a true game-time decision heading into Tuesday, but the Suns officially cleared him to play against Denver. According to ESPN, he was averaging 15.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 2.7 made three-pointers per game through six March appearances before being temporarily shut down.

item.title: Suns vs Spurs: Ultimate Breakdown of This High-Scoring Western Conference Showdown
item.description:
Devin Booker averaged 33.9 points per game over his last seven appearances heading into the final Suns vs Spurs matchup of the season — and yet Phoenix’s defense has been so porous that putting up 30-plus still might not be enough.

The Phoenix Suns and San Antonio Spurs met for the fourth and final time this regular season on Thursday, March 19, at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. With two of the Western Conference’s hottest offenses on the floor, the game had shootout written all over it.

item.title: Cameron Johnson's Surprising Rise Is Fueling the Nuggets' Playoff Push
item.description:
With about a month left in the NBA regular season, Cameron Johnson is finally starting to look like the player the Denver Nuggets envisioned when they acquired him. After battling injuries, adjusting to a new system, and admitting there is “still an element of figuring it out,” the veteran forward is stringing together his best stretch of basketball – and the timing could not be more important.

Quick Summary

  • Cameron Johnson has scored at least 15 points in three consecutive games, only the second time he has done that this season
  • He recently put up 18 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, a steal, and a block against the Lakers
  • Johnson has dealt with back spasms and an ankle injury, limiting his minutes in recent games
  • He is entering the final year of a $23.1 million contract and becomes extension-eligible this summer
  • The Denver Post called the Nuggets an “NBA Finals contender” when Johnson and Christian Braun find their groove

Cameron Johnson Admits He Is Still Adjusting to Denver

Honesty is refreshing in professional sports, and Johnson has been remarkably candid about his transition. Speaking to Bennett Durando of the Denver Post, the forward acknowledged that his first season with the Nuggets has required significant adjustment.

item.title: Kevin Durant MVP Push: Rockets Star Dominates at 37 With Historic Scoring Streak
item.description: At 37 years old, most NBA players are winding down their careers, accepting reduced roles, and mentoring younger teammates from the bench. Kevin Durant didn’t get that memo. The Houston Rockets forward is in the middle of one of the most remarkable late-career surges in league history, climbing into the top 10 of the MVP ladder and reminding everyone why he’s considered one of the greatest scorers to ever touch a basketball.

item.title: Mavericks vs Pelicans: Surprising Southwest Division Battle With Playoff Elimination Stakes
item.description:
The Dallas Mavericks have gone 4-19 over the last two months. The New Orleans Pelicans have gone 9-6 in their last 15 games. When these two Southwest Division rivals met at the Smoothie King Center on March 16, the contrast could not have been sharper — and neither could the stakes.

Key Takeaways

  • Dallas (23-45) entered on a 4-19 stretch over two months after officially embracing a tank strategy.
  • New Orleans (22-46) was riding its best stretch of basketball all season, going 9-6 in the last 15 games.
  • Cooper Flagg scored 27 points with 10 assists in Dallas’s shocking 130-120 upset of Cleveland the night before.
  • Dejounte Murray was listed as questionable due to illness after dropping a season-high 35 points against Houston.
  • Klay Thompson was downgraded to OUT, resting on the second night of a back-to-back.
  • The Pelicans led the season series 2-1 heading into this fourth and final meeting.

Mavericks vs Pelicans: A Tale of Two Trajectories

On paper, these teams look nearly identical. Dallas sat at 23-45, New Orleans at 22-46 — separated by just a single game near the bottom of the Western Conference. But the trajectories heading into Monday night told a completely different story.

item.title: Grizzlies vs Bulls: Essential Breakdown of a Pivotal Lottery Showdown
item.description:
When the Memphis Grizzlies rolled into the United Center to face the Chicago Bulls on March 16, neither team was playing for playoff glory. They were playing for something arguably just as valuable — lottery positioning.

Key Takeaways

  • Memphis (23-43) entered riding a brutal seven-game losing streak, the longest of their season.
  • Chicago (27-40) went winless in February and traded key role players at the deadline.
  • Only 3.5 games separated these two teams in the tank race, making every outcome critical for draft lottery odds.
  • Josh Giddey recorded three triple-doubles in his last four games, while Matas Buzelis scored 20+ points in six of his last eight contests.
  • Memphis listed six players as out with additional doubtful and questionable designations.

Grizzlies vs Bulls: Two Franchises at a Crossroads

This was the first meeting between the Grizzlies and Bulls all season, and the circumstances could not have been more dramatic. Memphis came in with the eighth-worst record in the league at 23-43, while Chicago sat at 27-40 — close enough to make every game a swing in the draft lottery calculus.

item.title: Derrick Jones Jr.'s Essential Role in the Clippers' 2026 Playoff Push
item.description:
A player once known primarily for slam dunk contests is quietly producing top-20 fantasy value and anchoring the Clippers’ defense during their playoff chase.

Quick Summary: Derrick Jones Jr. has emerged as the LA Clippers’ X-factor in their 2026 playoff push. He’s scored in double digits in 8 of his last 9 games, recorded 15 combined steals and blocks in 3 games, and has been described as delivering “elite two-way production.” However, recent injuries — including a head injury against the Knicks and a knee collision — have raised concerns about his availability down the stretch.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard Fuels Clippers' Stunning Turnaround After Disastrous Start
item.description:
Few players in NBA history have carried a team from the edge of irrelevance back into the playoff picture the way Kawhi Leonard is doing right now. After the LA Clippers lost 21 of their first 27 games this season, most analysts had already written their obituary. Leonard had other plans.

Key Takeaways

  • Kawhi Leonard is averaging 28.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game on elite shooting splits
  • The Clippers clawed back from a 6-21 start to reach .500 at 32-32, surpassing the Warriors for 8th in the Western Conference
  • An NBA investigation into a $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration has raised salary cap circumvention questions
  • Despite the turnaround, Leonard insists there is “nothing to be happy about” — the job is far from finished

Kawhi Leonard’s Monster Season by the Numbers

Leonard’s individual performance this season has been nothing short of extraordinary. At 34 years old, the two-time Finals MVP is putting up numbers that rival his peak seasons in San Antonio and Toronto.

item.title: Knicks vs Jazz Breakdown: Karl-Anthony Towns Dominates as New York Eyes Eastern Conference Surge
item.description:
Nobody in the NBA is collecting double-doubles faster than Karl-Anthony Towns right now, and the Utah Jazz are about to find out why.

The New York Knicks enter their March 11 matchup against the Utah Jazz riding a wave of momentum as one of the most dangerous teams in the Eastern Conference. At 41-25, they sit firmly in third place, while Utah limps into Madison Square Garden with a brutal 20-45 record near the bottom of the Western Conference. The last time these two teams met? The Knicks obliterated them 146-112 in December.
